sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
Exact registered transport definition for createRpcHost.plugins or ordinary PluginHost.use; acquisition begins only on installation.
base: Module URL used to resolve a relative `entry`.
command: Executable to run instead of `entry`, e.g. `python3`.
args: Arguments of `command`, or extra arguments.
cwd: Working-directory path passed to the native child launcher; controls child-process relative paths without changing the local module-resolution base.
env: `{ inherit, set }`: variable names to inherit and values to set.
wrap: Rewrites the computed launch command (e.g. to run inside `sandbox-exec` or `bwrap`) on every launch, restart and replace. Must keep stdin/stdout and environment, and forward the exit code.
stdio: stdio routing; default `{ stdin: "channel", stdout: "channel", stderr: "drain" }`.
limits: Limits such as `callWallTimeMs` per call.
permissions: Runtime permissions (Deno).
wire: `native` (default) or `jsonrpc` for other languages.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
token: Shared secret checked in the handshake; required for TCP, explicit socket paths and Windows pipes. Generate it per deployment and never log it.
Not set: named endpoints rely on OS user permissions.
offer: Optional local native handshake proposal for protocol versions, codecs and capabilities; only the actual two-sided exchange establishes the accepted agreement.
establish: Optional asynchronous handshake step receiving the raw byte or message channel and generation preparation options; authenticates and returns one ready remote channel.
supervision: Overrides the original supervisor restart, startup, stop and other policies; retains the same execution-unit owner without installing another supervisor.
onNotice: Receives expected launcher notices, such as the best-effort termination warning, instead of `report`.
onNotice.notice: The notice, usually `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` for `termination`.
Nothing; the notice is handled.
stdio.stdin: Route child input through the RPC channel or ignore it. Native stdio and bootstrap ownership remain with the process launcher.
`channel`: retain the channel input.
Use child stdin for the channel and bootstrap.
Ignore child stdin; do not select it for a stdin-based channel.
stdio.stdout: Select channel output, continuously drained output, or ignored output without changing the launcher owner.
`channel`: expose stdout as the RPC byte channel.
Reserve stdout for the byte channel.
Continuously consume stdout through the launcher output sink.
Discard stdout instead of exposing a channel.
stdio.stderr: Choose whether the native launcher drains or ignores child stderr; stderr is never the RPC response channel.
`drain`: consume stderr from process startup.
Drain stderr through the existing output sink.
Discard stderr without adding a reader.
limits.memoryBytes: Requested process memory limit in bytes, forwarded to the original supervisor and native launcher; unsupported enforcement follows the isolation policy.
Omitted: no explicit memory limit is requested.
limits.cpuTimeMs: Requested process CPU time limit in milliseconds; native enforcement depends on the chosen launcher capability and isolation policy.
Omitted: no explicit CPU time limit is requested.
limits.callWallTimeMs: Wall-clock cap for a call, consumed by the existing RPC caller rather than enforced as an operating-system process limit.
Omitted: no additional call wall-time cap is requested.
ipc: Configure the original per-connection pending-data/control limits and log sink. Explicit process features override only their matching IPC fields.
Omitted: keep the native IPC defaults unless an installed feature supplies that field.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
`defaultRpcReporter`, which reports through the default console path.
Route native process and background diagnostics to the application sink without printing credentials.
keyFactory: Application key generator for automatically keyed idempotent requests on managed spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core Peer assembly and do not consume this proxy field.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
Managed process spawn/connect consumes this policy for declared idempotent requests. A function source uses direct Core assembly and does not consume this proxy policy.
retryPort: Whole-invocation dispatch port for managed spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core Peer assembly and do not consume this field.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
verify: Listener side: `(auth, peer) => principalId` validating the client credential; throw to reject.
verify.auth: Portable credential from the incoming handshake, possibly undefined.
verify.peer: Handshake peer metadata supplied by the accepted transport.
Verified principal string or its Promise; throw or rejection refuses the candidate.
Not set: the `token` comparison is used.
Require an application principal for a listener rather than relying only on same-user socket permissions.
connectTimeoutMs: Original dial/named-lookup wait budget, separate from connect.timeoutMs handshake.
Omitted: original short-source default 5000 ms.
name: Application-selected local registration name, independent of remote self.name.
Omitted: original family registration name.
expose: Explicit method exposure list for an ordinary PluginHost installation; selects which existing methods that entry publishes without creating a local business implementation.
Omitted: original exposure policy.
connect: SDK handshake preparation options, not a second physical source.
Omitted: original handshake policy.
connect.timeoutMs: One finite nonnegative millisecond budget shared by identity and capability preparation; phases do not reset it, and it does not set business-call or task-stop deadlines.
Omitted: original source defaults.
spawn: Current entry, explicit entry, short options, or original full native source. No complete callable object is a raw source.
Absent in parent/connect/listen modes.
connectToParent: true only in the genuine native child, using actual first-frame authority.
Absent outside parent connection mode.
Adopt the actual parent bootstrap source.
connect.target: Explicit named, socket or original native outbound source.
Required in outbound connect mode only.
listen: Original named/socket listener admitting independent bidirectional sessions.
Absent outside listen mode.

usageSampleFailed: `PROCESS_USAGE_SAMPLE_FAILED`: CPU or memory sampling failed; show unavailable.
hostInvalidOption: `PROCESS_HOST_INVALID_OPTION`: a host option is invalid; fix the named field.
hostClosed: `PROCESS_HOST_CLOSED`: the outlet is releasing; use a new host or Peer.
handshakeTimeout: `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`: the handshake did not finish in time; open a new channel.
authRejected: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`: the credential was refused; do not retry with it.
channelClosed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`: work on a closed channel; reconnect and reconcile.
connectFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`: connecting to the other process, starting it, or setting up part of the channel failed. If the system call that starts the process or opens its streams throws, you get that same error object with its type, stack and fields intact. Its `source` becomes this package and its system `code` (such as `ENOENT`) becomes `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`, one stable value to check. An already wrapped failure keeps the original on `cause`.
listenFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED`: preparing to listen, or binding the listening address, failed. You receive the same system error object, with its type, stack and other fields unchanged; it only gains this package as `source` and `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED` as `code`. Both the reported error and the rejected promise keep the original `cause` chain.
pluginInvalidOption: `PROCESS_PLUGIN_INVALID_OPTION`: a plugin or source option is invalid.
resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.
connectionLimit: `PROCESS_CONNECTION_LIMIT`: connection, rate or payload limit; the call did not run.
instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.
healthPingFailed: `PROCESS_HEALTH_PING_FAILED`: a health ping failed; supervision restarts it.
terminalCall: `PROCESS_TERMINAL_CALL`: the registration is terminal and refuses calls.
liquidated: `PROCESS_LIQUIDATED`: the registration was liquidated; create a new one.

You receive the same system error object, with its type, stack and other fields unchanged; it only gains this package as `source` and `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED` as `code`. resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.

instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.
healthPingFailed: `PROCESS_HEALTH_PING_FAILED`: a health ping failed; supervision restarts it.
terminalCall: `PROCESS_TERMINAL_CALL`: the registration is terminal and refuses calls.
liquidated: `PROCESS_LIQUIDATED`: the registration was liquidated; create a new one.
